source.section: 8. What this does not prove: arbitrarily large one-step digit-sum collapse

target_statement: For every canonical ordinary-decimal realization of SeamAnnihilation.framedNine (2*r) at width 2*r+2, prove digitSum n = 9*r+10 and digitSum(step n)=2. Reuse the existing positive realization theorem to prove that for every natural B some positive finite seed has initial digitSum>B and next digitSum exactly2, with the same family also giving arbitrarily large canonical width.
interpretation: The ordinary-digit-sum scalar consequence is the new formalization. The family, realization, exact step value, and two-step palindrome behavior already exist. The manuscript is attributed to its original source; no new discovery is claimed.
hypotheses: The manuscript range even k>=2 is encoded by k=2*r and r>0 for the existential family.
Primary equality is universal over every canonical realization; any valid extension to r=0 must be explicit.
Original ordinary-decimal digitSum and Lychrel196.step are retained.
Quantified thresholds B include zero; canonical width refers to the same actual positive integer witness.
